span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Replacing the full matrix convolution by a rank-3 low-rank template decomposition cuts the number of filtering operations by the ratio of channel count to template rank, which is what makes near-realtime sorting of hundreds of channels possible
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Over-split clusters arise because the fitting algorithm splits a high-variance cluster across several templates in order to reduce total reconstruction error, which is why the resulting cluster pairs form one continuous density and can be merged automatically
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Manual operator curation is still needed despite the automatic merging heuristic, mainly because of electrode drift and other non-stationarities.
span.note: what this limits: any claim that the pipeline is automatic: OPERATOR CURATION IS STILL REQUIRED, PRIMARILY DUE TO NON-STATIONARITIES IN THE RECORDINGS SUCH AS ELECTRODE DRIFT
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The optimisation can settle in non-optimal local minima, which the authors only ameliorate by annealing several parameters.
span.note: what this limits: the reproducibility of a given sort: LIKE MOST CLUSTERING ALGORITHMS, THIS MODEL IS PRONE TO NON-OPTIMAL LOCAL MINIMA
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The speed comparison against the established framework was not run at the largest channel count, so no 384-channel baseline exists.
span.note: what this limits: the speed comparison as a guide at the largest channel counts: the established framework NEEDED 480 MINUTES TO SORT THE 32 CHANNEL RECORDING, AND 15,000 MINUTES (10 DAYS) TO SORT THE 128 CHANNEL RECORDING, and no 384-channel comparison was run
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The ground-truth spikes are the curated output of one of the two algorithms being compared.
span.note: what this limits: the accuracy comparison reported here: the hybrid ground truth data set was built from all the clusters of a recording previously analysed with KlustaKwik and curated by a human expert, and KlustaKwik is the algorithm Kilosort is compared against
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The accuracy benchmark was made by cropping a larger one.
span.note: what this limits: the 32-channel accuracy results: the authors detail only the 32 channel benchmarks, which they created by cropping the full 128 channel hybrid benchmark
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Scores are also reported after a best-possible merging step that no user could perform.
span.note: what this limits: any score quoted from this figure: panels g-i repeat the results after greedy best possible merges, and a further panel gives the number of merges required to reach the best score
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the denoised waveform SUBTRACTED from its original location after being added elsewhere
span.note: eliminates: an artificial increase in spike density at any point on the probe - a hybrid-data test that adds spikes without removing them changes the very statistic the sorter is being judged on

span.label: Kilosort represents the raw voltage as a sum of template waveforms triggered at spike times, which allows spatiotemporally overlapping spikes to be identified and resolved rather than missed.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Kilosort sorted 32-, 128- and 384-channel recordings in 10, 29 and 140 minutes on one GPU workstation, while KlustaKwik needed 480 minutes for the 32-channel and 15,000 minutes for the 128-channel recording on a CPU cluster.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On hybrid ground-truth data Kilosort yielded well-isolated units (score above 0.9) for 53% of ground-truth neurons versus 35% for KlustaKwik.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: After greedy best-possible operator merges Kilosort still led, 69% of units above score 0.9 against 60% for KlustaKwik.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Kilosort's accuracy advantage came from missing fewer spikes rather than from fewer false positives, which the authors attribute to its resolution of overlapping spikes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Fitting each spike with its own three-component spatiotemporal SVD ("private PCs") left about five times less residual waveform variance than one common per-channel PCA basis.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Kilosort's run time grows linearly with the number of recorded neurons rather than with channel count, so denser electrodes cost no extra processing time.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
